charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

corComponents.title: Combined operating ratio and its components
corComponents.content:
The combined operating ratio (COR) is the sum of the net claims ratio (claims incurred / net earned premium), net commission ratio (commissions paid to intermediaries / net earned premium) and expense ratio (operating expenses / net earned premium). Below 100% means the insurance book is underwriting-profitable before investment income.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: COR has improved from 95.9% (FY2022) to 91.9% (FY2025) largely on the claims ratio falling as pricing and reinsurance actions worked through; the expense ratio has instead drifted up (11.7% to 12.4%), so the claims line is doing all the work.

What to watch:

  • Which component is driving a COR change -- claims (pricing/reinsurance/weather), commission (channel mix) or expense (cost discipline)
  • Expense ratio creeping up even as headline COR improves
  • Catastrophe-heavy half-years distorting the claims ratio

underwritingResult.title: Underwriting result (legacy, pre-AASB17)
underwritingResult.content:
The underwriting result was the pre-AASB17 measure of profit purely from insurance operations -- net earned premium less net claims, commissions and expenses, excluding investment income.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: QBE stopped reporting this line after FY2021/H1-2022 when AASB 17 (effective FY2023) replaced it with the Insurance Service Result, which nets acquisition costs and discounting differently and is not directly comparable. Use the Insurance Service Result chart above for FY2022 onward.

What to watch:

  • The pre-2022 series only -- do not extend a trend line across the AASB17 transition
  • Swings driven by catastrophe years (FY2020 storms/COVID, FY2022 floods)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For QBE Insurance Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
